doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Freddie, Wayne, Cedar, Merritt lineup as his favorite
summary: Fuller calls this lineup the best, rehearsing parts on their own so Blakey knew the sound when he joined.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: There were several iterations of the Blakey group, but when you consider that you are in, in the first period before all the reunion stuff came back, do you consider the Freddie, Wayne, Merritt, joining-­

That was it. That was it for me. That's just my personal opinion, that band, we lived in breeze what we were doing. It's like we took a song last night, Wayne would call my room, "Curtis, could you come to my room? I want to run over this thing" boom, six in the morning and we are still running over that thing without Art. We did all that stuff without ever rehearsing with art. He came in and we pulled him in and, when he came in, once he heard it, he knew what it was supposed to sound like.
Then the other part of him would click in.
